Hi. We'll take this at your pace. Prop your phone side-on, a couple of metres back, so I can see all of you.
Plank. Forearms down, elbows under your shoulders, body in one straight line from your ears to your heels. It's completely normal to shake — that's the muscle working.
Knee plank. Same shape, knees down. Straight line from your ears to your knees.
Side plank on your knee. Elbow under your shoulder, lift your hips so you're straight from head to knees.
Dead bug. On your back, arms up, knees up. Lower one arm and the opposite leg slowly, keeping your lower back pressed flat into the floor. That flat back is the whole point.
Bird dog. On all fours. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back, until both are in line with your back. Imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back.
Glute bridge. On your back, knees bent, feet flat. Push through your heels and lift your hips into a straight ramp. Squeeze at the top.
Sit to stand. From a chair, no hands. Lean your chest forward, drive through your feet, stand all the way up. Sit back down slowly — that's the hard bit.
Wall sit. Back flat against a wall, slide down until your knees are bent at about a right angle. Then just hold.
Tucked hollow hold. On your back, knees pulled in, shoulders just off the floor. One job: press your lower back into the floor.
Crunch. On your back, knees bent. Peel your shoulder blades off the floor with your tummy — hands beside your head, never pulling on your neck.
Bent-knee leg raise. On your back, knees bent, lift them towards your chest and lower slowly. If your lower back lifts off the floor, you've gone too far.
Cat cow. On all fours. Round your back to the ceiling as you breathe out, then let it dip as you breathe in. Slow — this is a stretch, not an exercise. I'll breathe with you.
Downward dog. Hands and feet down, hips pushed up and back into an upside-down V. A long spine matters more than straight legs — bend your knees as much as you need.
Cobra. On your front, hands under your shoulders, gently lift your chest. Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears. This should feel good, never sharp.
